title: Evolution (Journey album) - Wikipedia
notes: March 1979; "the band's first album to feature drummer Steve Smith"; Aynsley Dunbar "was replaced with Smith, formerly with Ronnie Montrose's band"; "Lovin', Touchin', Squeezin'" their first top-20 hit (US 16), after Sam Cooke's "Nothing Can Change This Love". Personnel: Steve Smith, drums, percussion.

title: Enigmatic Ocean - Wikipedia
notes: Jean-Luc Ponty, 1977, number 1 on the Billboard jazz albums chart; Allan Holdsworth and Daryl Stuermer guitars, Allan Zavod keyboards, Ralphe Armstrong bass, Steve Smith drums and percussion. "Mirage" 4:53; its solos Ponty (violin) and Zavod (synthesizer); Smith solos on The Struggle of the Turtle to the Sea, Part III.

title: Steve Smith steps ahead on his Journey with Vital Information (George W. Harris, Jazz Weekly, 1 January 2018)
notes: "Buddy Rich, of course." "I saw Tony Williams play and there were certain phrases that he played that I wanted to learn, so I figured them out." "When I first saw Billy Cobham, his approach was a paradigm shift from my wanting to play the more Buddy Rich approach." "My gateway into fusion was by Jean-Luc Ponty ... I could combine the rock energy with jazz improvisation and odd time signatures, which his music required ... He was the one who asked me to buy a big double-bass drum set." On Journey: "I could bring that to the rock drumming in the band to add that certain kind of groove." On Zigaboo Modeliste: "I'll transcribe it and learn it." "I love to hear drummers with a nice touch that are able to draw a beautiful sound from the instrument."

title: Steve Smith & Vital Information: history (vitalinformation.com)
notes: Berklee, 1972-76, "where he had private lessons with both Gary Chaffee and Alan Dawson"; Jean-Luc Ponty's group and "the 1977 landmark fusion album" Enigmatic Ocean; asked to join Journey while touring with Ronnie Montrose; "Since 1983 Smith has led his own group Vital Information"; "In 1985 Smith left Journey to pursue his original passion, jazz."

title: Steve Smith's Journey 1980 Sonor Phonic set (Donn Bennett Drum Studio, the kit's sale)
notes: "Steve Smith first used this Sonor Phonic set on Journey's 1980 Departure tour"; it recorded "Dream After Dream 1980, Escape 1981, and Frontiers"; 9-ply beech shells in a natural oak veneer; "With Journey, Steve initially played two 24" bass drums, 12" and 13" rack toms with 16" and 18" floor toms, eventually adding the additional two rack toms" (8" and 10"); for jazz a single 20" bass drum. The set also recorded the first three Vital Information albums.

title: Drummer Steve Smith breaks down his drumming on the 1983 Journey song 'Separate Ways' (Laughing Squid, on his Drumeo lesson)
notes: Smith: "we wanted a song that had a powerful hook, a big sound, and had the effect to really rock the house"; the part arranged for arenas.

title: Journey - Don't Stop Believin' (Escape Tour 1981: Live in Houston), the band's channel
notes: The Summit, Houston, 6 November 1981, filmed for MTV; first released on video in November 2005 (Columbia/Legacy), remastered 2022. Its Who's Crying Now (2q4RwTIkYk0) and this upload were looked at for the likeness: long straight brown hair, clean-shaven, a pale pink V-neck T-shirt, a white sweatband, a red lacquered touring kit.
